01 / Overview

Brand foundation

Procedure EEF is positioned as a modern French education platform rather than a traditional study-abroad consultancy. The identity should feel premium through precision, clarity and restraint.

Brand

Procedure EEF

Primary mark

Custom geometric eef monogram

Master tagline

Études en France simplement

Visual character

Minimal, editorial, structured, intelligent, approachable, European/French in sensibility, digital-first and highly legible. Avoid generic student-agency clichés and excessive decorative treatment.

02 / Color

Core color system

The identity revolves around EEF Academic Blue, Academic Navy and Cool Mist. White and cool blue-grays support the system, while Deep Blue is reserved for controlled gradients, overlays and depth. Red/orange accents are intentionally excluded to keep the identity calm, academic and coherent.

04 / Logo

Logo system

One master geometry must be used everywhere. The two e forms, stroke widths, internal counters, connection geometry and f terminal construction are never to be independently redrawn.

Approved configurations

1Brand Mark / Monogram — eef symbol only.
2Primary Lockup — mark + Procedure EEF + master tagline.
3Horizontal Lockup — mark + wordmark aligned horizontally.
4Stacked / Vertical Lockup — mark above the wordmark.

Default

Academic Blue on Cool Mist

Dark

White on Academic Navy

Reversed

White on EEF Academic Blue

Monochrome

Academic Navy on Cool Mist / White

05 / Layout

Grid, spacing & geometry

Use oversized headlines, short text blocks, controlled asymmetry, generous negative space, fine rules and mathematically consistent alignment.

Whitespace

Whitespace is an active brand element. Avoid filling every area simply because space is available.

Logo engineering

Construction documentation should derive from actual geometry: baseline, reference unit, stroke, radii, counters, connection points and optical corrections.

Clear space

Define a measurable x-unit from the mark and repeat that minimum distance on all four sides. Do not use decorative x labels.

06 / Photography

France, without the cliché

Natural, editorial and recognizably French. Prioritize real student life, architecture, universities, apartments and arrival moments over tourism imagery or generic smiling stock portraits.

Use

Natural light, warm-neutral grading, authentic environments, editorial crops, consistent exposure and realistic detail.

Avoid

Tourist-postcard saturation, obvious AI artifacts, fake stock posing, excessive luxury treatment, cliché flags or generic education imagery.

07 / UI & Icons

Digital system

Cool Mist surfaces, white cards, Academic Navy typography, restrained academic-blue actions and a consistent rounded monoline icon system.

Surfaces

Cool Mist for branded backgrounds; White for floating cards, forms and high-clarity content surfaces.

Interaction

EEF Academic Blue for primary CTAs, selected navigation states, key icons and functional emphasis.

Icons

One grid, one optical size, one stroke width, one corner treatment and one visual weight.

08 / Applications

Brand in the real world

The identity should feel like a complete student ecosystem, not a decorative merchandise system.

Editorial / Print

Student guides, books, application folders, letterhead, notebooks and envelopes.

Identity objects

Student card, business card, badge and welcome-pack materials.

Merchandise

Tote, reusable bottle and hoodie only when execution is photorealistic, crisp and restrained.

Mockup production standard

Perspective-map the logo correctly. Use believable paper/fabric/material behavior, natural shadows and clean print/embroidery. No fuzzy branding, fake luxury effects or low-resolution mockups.

09 / Production

Technical delivery rules

The system must remain usable at agency and production level across PDF, web, print and UI output.

Vector-first

Logo, icons, UI geometry, rules and typography should remain vector/live wherever possible. Avoid unnecessary rasterization.

Raster quality

Photography and raster mockups should be high resolution and suitable for their final placed size; master-print assets should target 300 PPI at final size.

PDF output

Fonts embedded, selectable text, no low-resolution downsampling, no JPEG artifacts, one design page per PDF page.

Final QA

Inspect alignment, page rhythm, logo geometry, borders, radii, image sharpness, French accents, page numbering and clipping at multiple zoom levels.

Premium through precision and restraint — not through decoration.
